newsitem.title: MALDIVES: S.Asian nations want free trade by 2001 -India.
newsitem.headline: S.Asian nations want free trade by 2001 -India.

text.p: Seven south Asian nations have decided to move up a deadline for forming a free trade area by four years to 2001, Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday.

Gujral told a news conference on a resort island in the Maldives that leaders of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) reached the decision on the second day of a three-day summit.
The seven nation SAARC had previously pledged to form the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) by no later than 2005.
"We have decided that SAFTA must come in by 2001," Gujral said.
Gujral reiterated his satisfaction over talks on Monday with Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif, saying it was a "friendly meeting" and very cordial.
"Myself and prime minister Sharif do not expect dramatic results. It is encouraging we both say we need an improvement on the issues," Gujral said.
